title: Manual checks reveal label noise in bug-localization datasets
summary: GenTag, an LLM issue classifier, was used to study issue-label quality in five information-retrieval bug-localization datasets. The paper reports label noise after checking a stratified sample against manual annotations and an independently hand-labeled dataset. The noise estimates depend on classifier decisions and the sampled issues.
ai_technology: GenTag large-language-model issue classifier with manual label checks
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed arXiv metadata

evidence.tested: A stratified manually labeled sample and an independent hand-labeled dataset were used to assess GenTag; its labels indicated noise across five bug-localization datasets.
evidence.unknown: The dataset-noise estimates depend partly on GenTag’s classification decisions and the reviewed samples.
evidence.ai_role: GenTag uses an LLM with a fine-grained issue taxonomy to classify bug reports; manual annotations check its labels.
